Core_Headline: Why Competing Fonts Destroy Luxury Credibility
Diagnostic_Body: The fastest way to make a ₹50L architecture firm look like a ₹50k amateur is using 4 different fonts on your homepage. Never exceed 2 typefaces: one editorial serif for authority, one neutral geometric sans for reading.
Golden_Takeaway: Typography is not decoration. It is the visual tone of your voice before you speak.

Core_Headline: Tight Paragraphs Force High-Ticket Buyers to Bounce
Diagnostic_Body: When body text line-height drops below 1.5, reading on mobile becomes visual manual labor. High-net-worth clients won't squint through cramped text—they close the tab in 3 seconds.
Golden_Takeaway: Give your sentences room to breathe. Generous leading signals calm confidence.

Core_Headline: If Everything Shouts, Nothing Gets Heard
Diagnostic_Body: When subheadings and body copy are nearly identical in size, the eye wanders without an anchor. High-converting executive design demands dramatic mathematical contrast: H1 (56px) -> H2 (32px) -> H3 (22px) -> Body (16px).
Golden_Takeaway: Scale creates immediate hierarchy. Hierarchy dictates reading priority.

Rule_Header: RULE #04: THE CURSE OF ALL-CAPS BODY TEXT
Core_Headline: Stop Shouting at High-Net-Worth Prospects
Diagnostic_Body: ALL-CAPS sentences reduce reading speed by 38% because the eye loses recognizable letter ascenders and descenders. Reserve uppercase strictly for small 10-12px tracking pills and micro-kickers.
Golden_Takeaway: Uppercase is for precision labels. Sentence case is for persuasion.

Core_Headline: Why Long Text Lines Kill Mobile Reading Flow
Diagnostic_Body: The optimal line length for readability is 45 to 75 characters. When a line stretches across a wide desktop screen with 120 characters, the reader's eye gets lost tracking back to the next line.
Golden_Takeaway: Constrain your text containers. Controlled reading width keeps attention locked.

Core_Headline: Low-Contrast Grey Text Is An Incompetence Signal
Diagnostic_Body: Light grey text (#888888) on white backgrounds might look trendy on Dribbble, but it fails WCAG accessibility and frustrates mature decision-makers reading in direct sunlight.
Golden_Takeaway: Luxury is never illegible. Enforce a minimum 7:1 contrast ratio on all core copy.

Core_Headline: The Editorial Pairing Used by Luxury Heritage Houses
Diagnostic_Body: Pairing an evocative high-contrast serif (Fraunces or Playfair) with a hyper-clean sans-serif (Inter) creates instant boardroom gravitas. The serif delivers provenance; the sans delivers speed.
Golden_Takeaway: Proven editorial pairing bridges centuries of craft with modern digital agility.

Core_Headline: Why Decorative Script Fonts Cheapen High-End Services
Diagnostic_Body: Using ornate faux-calligraphy fonts for clinic or interior headers makes your firm look like a craft hobby shop. It signals amateur design templates bought for $19.
Golden_Takeaway: If a client cannot read your headline in 400ms, your branding has failed.

Core_Headline: Letter-Spacing on Small Headers Signals Intentionality
Diagnostic_Body: Expanding tracking (letter-spacing: +0.08em) on small 12px uppercase category kickers creates immediate architectural order. It frames the content like a museum label.
Golden_Takeaway: Letter-spacing small uppercase labels turns text into a precision badge.

Core_Headline: Why Inconsistent Margins Cause Subconscious Anxiety
Diagnostic_Body: When space above a heading is 40px and below is 15px, but the next section has 60px and 30px, the human brain registers cognitive disorder. Set an unbreakable 8px spacing grid across the entire page.
Golden_Takeaway: Consistency in whitespace rhythm breeds subconscious trust before words register.

Core_Headline: Displaying Numbers with Monospace Precision
Diagnostic_Body: When presenting metrics, pricing, or turnaround times, use tabular figures or a monospace accent. Numbers set in monospaced glyphs feel engineered, verified, and mathematically true.
Golden_Takeaway: Tabular numbers convey institutional precision. Proportional numbers feel subjective.

Core_Headline: Single Trailing Words Ruin Layout Symmetry
Diagnostic_Body: A single word sitting on its own line at the end of a headline or paragraph creates an awkward visual gap that drags the eye down. Balance your headline breaks intentionally.
Golden_Takeaway: Eliminate dangling orphans. Balanced paragraph blocks signal obsessive craftsmanship.

Core_Headline: When You Bold Everything, Nothing Carries Weight
Diagnostic_Body: Websites that bold every third word look like aggressive sales flyers. In executive design, bolding is reserved strictly for the core transformation phrase—never whole paragraphs.
Golden_Takeaway: Bolding is a scalpel, not a paintbrush. Use it with surgical restraint.

Core_Headline: The 7-Word Ceiling for Luxury First Impressions
Diagnostic_Body: If your homepage hero headline is a 35-word run-on paragraph, the visitor's eye will skip it entirely. High-ticket authority is stated with supreme brevity: under 8 words, perfectly set.
Golden_Takeaway: Brevity is the ultimate signal of confidence. Long explanations signal insecurity.

Core_Headline: The Hidden FOUT Glitch That Ruins First Visits
Diagnostic_Body: When your custom serif takes 2 seconds to load, your visitor sees an unstyled Times New Roman flicker. Always subset your woff2 fonts and match fallback font metrics exactly.
Golden_Takeaway: Invisible typography engineering prevents brand-destroying layout shifts.

Core_Headline: Transforming Boring Project Names Into Asset Titles
Diagnostic_Body: Replacing 'Project Whitefield' with 'The ₹12Cr Whitefield Penthouse: Turnkey Materiality Teardown' commands 3x higher perceived competence before the client views the images.
Golden_Takeaway: Contextual titling elevates a portfolio gallery into an institutional case study.

Core_Headline: Testimonial Cards Must Look Like Architectural Inscriptions
Diagnostic_Body: Standard quote marks look dated. Style pull-quotes in an enlarged, elegant serif with a subtle vertical hairline bar and author credentials set in clean tabular sans.
Golden_Takeaway: A well-set pull-quote looks like a verified endorsement from an executive board.

Core_Headline: Balancing Regular, Medium, and SemiBold Across the Screen
Diagnostic_Body: 60% of your text should sit at regular weight (400), 30% at medium (500) for UI/labels, and 10% at bold/semibold (600) for focal hooks. Heavy weights across 50% of the screen feel suffocating.
Golden_Takeaway: Weight contrast guides ocular navigation effortlessly down the conversion funnel.

Core_Headline: Why High-End Pricing Should Never Look Like an E-Commerce Tag
Diagnostic_Body: Slashing a red price tag next to an inflated number screams discount warehouse. Elite services present investment parameters with quiet typography: structured tiers, exact inclusions, zero starbursts.
Golden_Takeaway: Dignified pricing typography eliminates the urge to haggle.

Core_Headline: Form Field Labels and Button Copy Dictate Trust
Diagnostic_Body: Replacing 'Submit' with 'Request Private Consultation' changes user psychology from feeling processed to feeling prioritized. Every micro-button copy must reflect executive deference.
Golden_Takeaway: Micro-copy is where user friction either dissolves or converts into a lost lead.

Core_Headline: Why 48px Desktop Titles Break on iPhone Screens
Diagnostic_Body: A title that looks commanding on a 27-inch monitor wraps into 5 awkward lines on an iPhone screen. Employ responsive fluid typography (clamp) so headlines never break into awkward fragments.
Golden_Takeaway: Responsive typography ensures board-level visual poise on any pocket screen.

Core_Headline: Inconsistent Navigation Capitalization Destroys Credibility
Diagnostic_Body: Mixing 'About us', 'PORTFOLIO', and 'Contact Us' in the same navigation bar reveals sloppy attention to detail. Pick Title Case or Small Caps and lock it across all interactive chrome.
Golden_Takeaway: Meticulous consistency across minor navigation points signals rigorous engineering.

Core_Headline: Standard Rounded Bullets Look Like 1998 Word Documents
Diagnostic_Body: Replace standard browser bullets with delicate typographic dashes (—), custom micro-plus icons, or numbered tabular accents. It instantly modernizes your feature lists.
Golden_Takeaway: Custom typographic list markers elevate simple bullet points into premium specifications.

Core_Headline: Using True Italic Glyphs for Emotional Nuance
Diagnostic_Body: Slanted faux-italics generated by browsers look distorted. Use fonts with designed true italics to highlight a single word of philosophy or quiet provenance.
Golden_Takeaway: True italics add editorial warmth and intellectual texture to cold commercial copy.

Core_Headline: The 1.8 Line-Height Subtitle That Keeps Visitors Reading
Diagnostic_Body: Your hero subtitle must be set at exactly 18-20px with 1.7 to 1.8 line-height. This creates a relaxed reading rhythm that guides the user directly into your primary proof point.
Golden_Takeaway: A relaxed subtitle rhythm lowers cognitive resistance and keeps the thumb scrolling.

Core_Headline: Pairing Big Numbers with Micro-Labels
Diagnostic_Body: When showcasing '₹45Cr' or '99.4%', scale the number to 64px in a bold serif and pair it with a 12px uppercase muted label below. The scale differential creates instant visual impact.
Golden_Takeaway: Dramatic scale contrast between metrics and labels makes proof undeniable.

Core_Headline: The Final Scroll Must Look Like an Architectural Colophon
Diagnostic_Body: Most footers are cluttered link dumps. Style your footer like an architectural monograph: discreet legal lines, quiet navigation columns, and a clean brand hallmark.
Golden_Takeaway: A serene footer leaves the visitor with a lingering impression of institutional permanence.

Core_Headline: Why Centered Long Copy Is A Visual Disaster
Diagnostic_Body: Centering more than 3 lines of body text forces the reader's eye to hunt for a different starting point on every single line. Keep body text left-aligned with a hard, disciplined margin.
Golden_Takeaway: Left alignment provides a rigid ocular anchor. Centered text creates reading fatigue.

Core_Headline: Never Use Pure Black (#000000) on Pure White
Diagnostic_Body: Pure black text on pure white creates harsh optical vibration. Use deep charcoal (#1A1917 or #141413) on warm off-white (#FBF9F5). It softens optical strain and feels luxurious.
Golden_Takeaway: Editorial charcoal on warm bone is the signature palette of museum monographs.

Core_Headline: Design Is Complete Not When There Is Nothing More to Add
Diagnostic_Body: Elite visual design is achieved when you can remove nothing further without compromising the message. Strip away every redundant font, drop shadow, and decorative line.
Golden_Takeaway: Purity is the highest form of sophistication. Eliminate until only authority remains.
